question: Does extending generative (Transformer) language model pretraining to many languages, with monolingual and parallel-data objectives, improve cross-lingual classification, machine translation and low-resource language modeling?
hypothesis: Pretraining a shared Transformer with cross-lingual language modeling objectives (CLM, MLM, and TLM when parallel data exists) gives better cross-lingual representations and better initialisation for NLU and MT than prior approaches.
contributions: A new unsupervised method for learning cross-lingual representations using cross-lingual language modeling, investigating two monolingual pretraining objectives.
A new supervised learning objective (TLM) that improves cross-lingual pretraining when parallel data is available.
Significantly outperforms the previous state of the art on cross-lingual classification, unsupervised machine translation and supervised machine translation.
Cross-lingual language models give significant perplexity improvements for low-resource languages.
Code and pretrained models to be made public.

method.summary: A single Transformer with a shared BPE vocabulary across languages is pretrained with CLM, MLM (BERT-style but on 256-token streams of many sentences) or MLM+TLM (MLM on concatenated parallel sentence pairs with reset target positions and language embeddings). The pretrained model initialises XNLI fine-tuning, encoder/decoder of unsupervised and supervised NMT, a Nepali LM, and yields word embeddings.
method.task: cross-lingual language model pretraining (MLM / CLM / TLM) with downstream XNLI, unsupervised and supervised MT, low-resource LM

datasets.name: Wikipedia dumps (monolingual, XNLI languages)
datasets.preprocessing: Moses tokenizer (Kytea for Japanese, Chang et al. 2008 for Chinese, PyThaiNLP for Thai), fastBPE codes learned on sentences sampled from all languages with multinomial alpha=0.5

datasets.name: Parallel data for TLM (English-X only)
datasets.source: MultiUN (fr, es, ru, ar, zh), IIT Bombay (hi), OPUS: EUbookshop (de, el, bg), OpenSubtitles 2018 (tr, vi, th), Tanzil (ur, sw), GlobalVoices (sw)

datasets.name: XNLI
datasets.split: fine-tune on English MultiNLI, test zero-shot on 15 XNLI languages

datasets.name: WMT'14 en-fr, WMT'16 en-de, WMT'16 en-ro
Nepali Wikipedia (plus Hindi and English)
datasets.size: about 100k Nepali sentences; Hindi about 6 times more
datasets.preprocessing: shared BPE vocabulary of 100k subword units for this experiment

datasets.name: MUSE dictionaries and SemEval'17 cross-lingual word similarity
datasets.source: Conneau et al. 2018a; Camacho-Collados et al. 2017

models.name: XLM (CLM / MLM / MLM+TLM)
models.architecture: Transformer encoder with GELU, learned positional embeddings, language embeddings
models.vocab: 95k for XNLI model (80k BPE splits); 100k BPE units in Nepali experiment

models.name: Artetxe and Schwenk 2018 (LASER-style)
models.architecture: shared LSTM encoder, trained on 223 million parallel sentences

models.name: Lample et al. 2018b unsupervised MT (NMT, PBSMT)

training.objective: CLM: P(w_t | w_1..w_{t-1}); MLM: 15% of BPE tokens selected, 80% [MASK], 10% random, 10% unchanged, frequent outputs subsampled with weights proportional to sqrt of inverse frequency; TLM: MLM on concatenated parallel sentences with masks in both, target positions reset. MT fine-tuning: denoising auto-encoding plus online back-translation (unsupervised).
training.lr: 1e-4 to 5e-4 (pretraining); sampled from 5e-4 to 2e-4 for XNLI fine-tuning
training.batch_size: CLM/MLM: 64 streams of 256 tokens; TLM: 4000 tokens of similar-length sentences; MT: 2000 tokens; XNLI fine-tune: 8 or 16
training.hardware: 64 Volta GPUs for language modeling, 8 GPUs for MT tasks

other.stopping: averaged perplexity over languages as stopping criterion
other.language_sampling_for_bpe: q_i = p_i^alpha / sum_j p_j^alpha, p_i = n_i / sum_k n_k, alpha = 0.5
other.language_sampling_for_batches: same distribution with alpha = 0.7; each batch from one language; TLM alternates with MLM and samples language pairs similarly
other.xnli_eval_epochs: small evaluation epochs of 20000 random samples
other.xnli_pooling: first hidden state of last layer into randomly initialised linear classifier, all parameters fine-tuned; max/mean pooling not better
other.mlm_input: streams of arbitrary number of sentences truncated at 256 tokens, not sentence pairs
other.clm_context: first words of each batch left without context (no hidden-state passing)

inference.samples: single reported number per cell; no seeds or runs stated

eval.protocol: Zero-shot cross-lingual transfer on XNLI (train English, test 15 languages) plus translate-train and translate-test; 9 encoder/decoder init combinations for unsupervised MT; no significance tests or seeds reported.

We use 80k BPE splits and a vocabulary of 95k and train a 12-layer model on the Wikipedias of the XNLI languages.

results.claim: Supervised XLM (MLM+TLM) reaches a new XNLI zero-shot average accuracy.
results.setup: Train on English MultiNLI, zero-shot on 15 XNLI languages; 12-layer, 1024 hidden XLM pretrained on Wikipedia plus English-X parallel data; baseline Artetxe and Schwenk 2018 with 223M parallel sentences.
results.quote: improving even further the state of the art to 75.1%
results.note: Abstract and conclusion say 4.9% absolute gain over previous SOTA (75.1 vs 70.2).

results.claim: Unsupervised MLM-only XLM beats the supervised Artetxe and Schwenk encoder on XNLI.
results.quote: MLM obtains 71.5% accuracy on average (∆), while they obtained 70.2% accuracy.

results.claim: Adding TLM to MLM boosts XNLI average accuracy by 3.6 points.
results.quote: we get a significant boost in performance of 3.6% accuracy

results.claim: TLM raises English XNLI accuracy from 83.2 to 85.0.
results.setup: XLM MLM vs MLM+TLM, English test.
results.quote: Using TLM in addition to MLM also improves English accuracy from 83.2% to 85% accuracy

results.claim: Fine-tuning on translated train sets (TRANSLATE-TRAIN) gives the best XNLI average.
results.quote: reaching an absolute state of the art of 76.7% average accuracy

results.claim: XLM MLM+TLM TRANSLATE-TEST XNLI average is 74.2, below zero-shot 75.1.
results.table: Table 1, row XLM (MLM+TLM) under TRANSLATE-TEST, column delta

results.claim: Unsupervised MT: best model (MLM encoder and decoder) reaches 34.3 BLEU on de-en, more than 9 BLEU over the previous best.
results.setup: Encoder and decoder both initialised with MLM pretraining, then denoising auto-encoding plus online back-translation; 6-layer model, 2000-token batches; baseline Lample et al. 2018b PBSMT+NMT.
results.quote: In German-English, our best model outperforms the previous unsupervised approach by more than 9.1 BLEU, and 13.3 BLEU if we only consider neural unsupervised approaches.

results.claim: Unsupervised MT en-fr and fr-en best BLEU with MLM/MLM init.
results.setup: MLM/MLM init; en-fr 33.4, fr-en 33.3; baseline best prior en-fr PBSMT 28.1.
results.table: Table 2, row MLM MLM, columns en-fr and fr-en

results.claim: MLM pretraining beats CLM pretraining for unsupervised MT.
results.quote: going from 30.4 to 33.4 BLEU on English-French, and from 28.0 to 31.8 on Romanian-English

results.claim: Pretraining the encoder and decoder with MLM beats pretraining only the lookup table (EMB) by up to 7 BLEU on de-en.
results.quote: leads to consistent significant improvements of up to 7 BLEU on German-English

results.claim: The encoder is the most important component to pretrain for unsupervised MT.

results.claim: Supervised MT ro-en: MLM-pretrained bidirectional model with back-translation reaches new SOTA.
results.setup: MLM pretraining, ro<->en + BT; back-translation uses the same monolingual data as pretraining; baseline Sennrich et al. 2016 (back-translation + ensemble).
results.quote: Our bidirectional model trained with back-translation obtains the best performance and reaches 38.5 BLEU

results.claim: Supervised MT ro-en unidirectional: no pretraining 28.4, CLM 31.5, MLM 35.3.
Nepali perplexity falls from 157.2 to 109.3 when adding English and Hindi data.

limits: No seeds, variance or significance tests reported; single numbers per cell.
Number of parameters, training steps, tokens, corpus sizes and compute hours are not given; warmup length and weight decay unstated.
Learning rate is given only as a range and appears to be tuned per task.
TLM requires English-centric parallel data; coverage differs by language pair (MultiUN, OPUS corpora of different domains).
XNLI comparison with Artetxe and Schwenk uses a different pretraining data regime (223M parallel sentences vs Wikipedia), and TLM adds parallel data, so MLM and MLM+TLM are not equal-data.
EMB baseline was reimplemented and beat the published numbers; authors attribute this to larger batches.
Nepali gains are shown only for Wikipedia-scale data and one low-resource language; explanation (shared anchor n-grams) is offered, not tested.
Text is the arXiv v1; XLM-R and later multilingual models have superseded the specific numbers.

terms.definition: a Transformer language model trained to model the probability of a word given the previous words in a sentence
BERT's objective (Cloze task) applied to streams of text: 15% of BPE tokens sampled, replaced by [MASK] 80%, random 10%, unchanged 10%
extension of MLM that concatenates parallel sentences and masks words in both so the model can use the other language as context; target positions are reset
the English MultiNLI training set is machine translated into each XNLI language
every dev and test set of XNLI is translated to English

figures.caption: Cross-lingual language model pretraining. The MLM objective is similar to the one of Devlin et al. (2018), but with continuous streams of text as opposed to sentence pairs. The TLM objective extends MLM to pairs of parallel sentences. To predict a masked English word, the model can attend to both the English sentence and its French translation, and is encouraged to align English and French representations. Position embeddings of the target sentence are reset to facilitate the alignment.
figures.why: Shows token + position + language embeddings summed and the TLM English/French concatenation with reset positions; clearest picture of MLM vs TLM.

figures.caption: Results on cross-lingual classification accuracy. Test accuracy on the 15 XNLI languages.
figures.why: Per-language XNLI results for MLM vs MLM+TLM against mBERT and LASER-style baselines.

figures.caption: Results on unsupervised MT. BLEU scores on WMT'14 English-French, WMT'16 German-English and WMT'16 Romanian-English.
figures.why: Grid of nine encoder/decoder init choices (-, EMB, CLM, MLM) showing MLM and encoder pretraining matter most.
